title: CAOS: Conformal Aggregation of One-Shot Predictors
claim: Our aggregated method yields consistently smaller uncertainty sets than split baselines, approaching the oracle's efficiency per item.
layout: 1 panel scatter plot, diagonal oracle line, legend bottom-right
description: A single scatter plot compares prediction set size per landmark. The x-axis is the set size for the SCOS oracle, from 0 to 25, and the y-axis is the set size for each method, also from 0 to 25. A dashed gray diagonal marks the SCOS Oracle, where y equals x. Hollow dark-gray circles for SCOS sit far above the diagonal, in the upper left. Light blue triangles for SCOS Best sit above the line but lower than the circles. Pink-maroon diamonds for CAOS [ours] cluster near or below the diagonal, mostly in the low range of 5 to 12. A legend in the lower right names the four series. The eye goes first to the dense pink cluster near the diagonal and then to the gap above it.
caption: Prediction set size per landmark for exemplar-based facial landmarking. Each point corresponds to a landmark. CAOS yields smaller prediction sets than SCOS and SCOS Best, approaching oracle efficiency.
abstract: One-shot prediction enables rapid adaptation of pretrained foundation models to new tasks using only one labeled example, but lacks principled uncertainty quantification. While conformal prediction provides finite-sample coverage guarantees, standard split conformal methods are inefficient in the one-shot setting due to data splitting and reliance on a single predictor. We propose Conformal Aggregation of One-Shot Predictors (CAOS), a conformal framework that adaptively aggregates multiple one-shot predictors and uses a leave-one-out calibration scheme to fully exploit scarce labeled data. Despite violating classical exchangeability assumptions, we prove that CAOS achieves valid marginal coverage using a monotonicity-based argument. Experiments on one-shot facial landmarking and RAFT text classification tasks show that CAOS produces substantially smaller prediction sets than split conformal baselines while maintaining reliable coverage.
